standard_prerequisites.name: Connection
standard_prerequisites.statement: A connection of an interval exchange transformation is a finite orbit fragment joining two discontinuities.
standard_prerequisites.use: The statement asserts the existence of a centre lying in no non-trivial connection.

standard_prerequisites.name: Centres and connections
standard_prerequisites.statement: Any non-trivial irreducible connection contains at most one point from the set of middle points of the exchanged intervals.
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies a centre that is not in any connection.

standard_prerequisites.name: Minimality of ergodic interval exchange transformations
standard_prerequisites.statement: An ergodic interval exchange transformation is minimal, so the orbit of every point is dense.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces an iterate of an endpoint close to the chosen centre.

core_obligations: Use the corollary on centres and connections to find a centre that belongs to no connection of the transformation, and the corollary on infinite connection times together with ergodicity to control the index (source line 734).
Use minimality to find a positive exponent for which a backward iterate of a chosen endpoint lies within half of a small parameter of that centre (source lines 736-739).

Shrink the parameter so that it is below the minimum length of the exchanged intervals and so that the symmetric interval about the centre of that radius avoids the relevant discontinuities (source line 740).

Apply the endpoint-iteration lemma to the interval spanned by the backward and forward iterates of the endpoints, which is then symmetric about the chosen centre, and read off the disjointness conclusion (source line 742).

proof_roadmap.step: Choose a centre that lies in no connection and control its index.
Approximate the centre by a backward iterate of an endpoint and shrink the parameter.
Apply the endpoint-iteration lemma to obtain a symmetric interval about the centre.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 728-731: for an ergodic symmetric interval exchange transformation there is an exchanged-interval index whose centre lies in no non-trivial connection and such that, for every sufficiently small positive parameter, a symmetric interval of that radius about the centre is contained in the exchanged interval and avoids the relevant set. The proof (source lines 733-743) assembles three earlier results that the statement does not mention: the corollary bounding how many centres a connection may contain, the corollary on infinite connection times together with ergodicity, and minimality, which is used to approximate the chosen centre by a backward iterate of an endpoint; only then does the endpoint-iteration lemma turn that approximation into a symmetric interval about the centre, after the parameter has been shrunk below the minimum length of the exchanged intervals.
